overview: The Medford City Council met to address various administrative tasks, licensing, and community issues, including a severe rat infestation at Brooks Park Apartments and zoning amendments for affordable housing. The council approved several litigation settlements, board appointments, and a ban on face surveillance technology.

items.title: Resolution Congratulating Library Director Barbara Kerr
items.summary: The Council approved a resolution congratulating Library Director Barbara Kerr on her retirement, amending it to request that the Library Trustees name a space in the library after her.

items.title: Approval of Meeting Records
items.summary: The Council tabled the records for the March 24, 2026 meeting and approved the records for the March 31, 2026 special joint meeting.

items.title: Committee of the Whole Reports
items.summary: The Council approved reports from the April 1, 2026 Committee of the Whole meeting concerning snow removal and litigation.

items.title: Grant of Location: 3960 Mystic Valley Parkway
items.summary: Following a public hearing, the Council approved National Grid's petition to relocate a utility pole at 3960 Mystic Valley Parkway with conditions recommended by the engineering division.

items.title: Common Victualler License: Cilantro's Mexican Grill
items.summary: The Council approved a common victualler license for Cilantro's Mexican Grill at 495 Riverside Avenue with extended operating hours up to midnight, subject to a 30, 60, and 90-day review.

items.title: Resolution Regarding Brooks Park Apartments Rat Infestation
items.summary: Residents of Brooks Park Apartments shared experiences regarding a severe rat infestation, leading the Council to pass a resolution to formally pressure property manager Charlesgate and request enforcement options from city health and building departments.

items.title: Inclusionary Zoning for Fractional Affordable Housing Incentives
items.summary: The Council referred a proposed zoning amendment to the Community Development Board that would allow developers to make fractional payments to the Affordable Housing Trust Fund instead of rounding up to build a whole affordable unit.

items.title: Tabling of Papers 26073 and 26058
items.summary: The Council voted to table papers 26073 and 26058 to be considered at a special meeting the following week.

items.title: Executive Session Litigation Settlements
items.summary: The Council approved several municipal litigation settlements totaling over $300,000 as recommended following an executive session on April 1, 2026.

items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
items.summary: The Council approved appointments to the Conservation Commission, the Elections Commission, the Garden Commission, and the Zoning Board of Appeals.

items.title: Capital Stabilization Fund Appropriation for Election Equipment
items.summary: The Council approved an appropriation of $13,800 from the Capital Stabilization Fund for 20 new pole pads and related election expenses.

items.title: Third Reading: Face Surveillance Technology Ban
items.summary: The Council approved the third reading of a proposed ordinance banning face surveillance technology.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Members of the public spoke to the council regarding the upcoming May Day holiday and expressed concern over the city's ability to enforce sanitation and rodent control laws.
